title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a tower X --f--> S --g--> T with f smooth. He notes in a bracket that 'differentially smooth' (EGA 0_IV 20.5) would suffice to make (1) exact. Smoothness gives the exact sequence of locally free modules (1) 0 → f*Ω^1_{S/T} → Ω^1_{X/T} → Ω^1_{X/S} → 0.

Taking exterior powers gives the Koszul-type filtration Fil^p_{X/S} on Ω^•_{X/T}: Fil^p is the image of f*Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗ Ω^{•-p}_{X/T}. Its graded pieces are (2) Gr^p = f*Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗ Ω^•_{X/S}[-p].

The filtration is stable under the de Rham differential, and (2) is compatible with differentials. The marginal insertion explains how the right-hand side gets a differential: f*Ω^p_{S/T} carries a canonical integrable connection relative to X/S. Equivalently it is f^{-1}Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗_{f^{-1}O_S} Ω^•_{X/S}, with differential 1⊗d.

Since f is flat and Ω^•_{X/S} is flat, he rewrites (2) as (2') Gr^p ≃ Lf*Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗^L Ω^•_{X/S}[-p]. He adds the caveat 'dans la mesure où cela veut dire quelque chose', because the differentials are only f^{-1}O_S-linear, not O_X-linear.

The filtration then makes Rf_*Ω^•_{X/T} an object of a filtered derived category, with Gr_{X/S}. The next page carries this through:
- Gr commutes with Rf_*.
- The projection formula gives (3) Gr^p Rf_* ≃ Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S}[-p].
- The connecting map Gr^p → Gr^{p+1}[1] yields d_1.
- At p=0, d_1 is the Gauss–Manin connection; d_1∘d_1 = 0 gives integrability.

This is exactly Katz–Oda (1968), with the E_1 spectral-sequence differential replaced by a morphism in the filtered derived category. Purpose: to set up Gauss–Manin connections, and then Picard–Fuchs equations and Cartier operators, for the dossier this page belongs to. The derived-level version gives a 'connection' on the complex Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S} itself, not only on its cohomology sheaves.
errors: (2') as written is not literally meaningful in D(O_X): the graded pieces are complexes whose differentials are not O_X-linear. Grothendieck flags this himself ('dans la mesure où cela veut dire quelque chose'). The correct formulation is f^{-1}Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗_{f^{-1}O_S} Ω^•_{X/S}, i.e. one works over f^{-1}O_S. The projection formula on the next page is correspondingly 'pas très catholique'.

Differential smoothness suffices for left exactness of (1) only with suitable finiteness/flatness hypotheses. Also, flatness of f (used for Lf* = f*) is not automatic for 'differentially smooth' without further hypotheses. This is minor.

At the derived level, d_1∘d_1 = 0 in the derived category does not by itself give a well-defined integrable connection on a complex, since homotopies matter. The next-page margin acknowledges a missing compatibility check. On cohomology sheaves the classical Katz–Oda result is correct.

ideas.what: Koszul filtration of Ω^•_{X/T} induced by f*Ω^1_{S/T} ⊂ Ω^1_{X/T}, with graded pieces f*Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗ Ω^•_{X/S}[-p]
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Katz and T. Oda (1968); Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (1970)

ideas.what: Gauss–Manin connection as the d_1 differential, lifted to a morphism in the filtered derived category, with integrability from d_1^2 = 0
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection via the filtered derived category / E_1 differential
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Oda (spectral-sequence form); Illusie (filtered derived categories, 1971–72); derived/∞-categorical versions much later
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's own crystalline definition is in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); this filtered-derived reformulation: unsure

ideas.what: Pullback f*E carries a canonical integrable connection relative to X/S, giving the differential on f*Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗ Ω^•_{X/S}
ideas.modern_name: relative de Rham complex of a pulled-back module (f^{-1}-linear structure)

ideas.what: Remark that this connection seems to agree with the one he defined himself (crystalline)
ideas.modern_name: comparison of Katz–Oda and crystalline Gauss–Manin connections

missed.claim: He aims to make the Gauss–Manin connection live on the complex Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S} as an object of a filtered derived category, not just on its cohomology. He notes that a compatibility (homotopy coherence) must still be proved, and leaves it there. This is essentially what later derived/∞-categorical treatments do (Gauss–Manin as a derived crystal or D-module structure).
missed.quote: La filtration sur Ω^•_{X/T} définit Rf_*(Ω^•_{X/T}) comme objet d'une catégorie dérivée filtrée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only. The derived Gauss–Manin connection is now standard in the derived-de Rham / ∞-categorical literature, so nothing here is new mathematically.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful re-derivation of Katz–Oda, explicitly credited to them, with a mild filtered-derived-category upgrade and self-flagged gaps. It is routine for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The marginal insertion reads approximately: 'compte tenu que, grâce à la connexion intégrable de f*(Ω^p_{S/T}) rel. X/S, f*(Ω^p_{S/T}) ⊗ Ω^•_{X/S} est muni d'une différentielle'. The fragment 'sur : la composante de' should be 'grâce à la connexion intégrable de'.
In (2), the argument of Gr was corrected in the manuscript to Ω^•_{X/T}.
The last term of (1) is Ω^1_{X/S}, corrected in the manuscript; the left end is likely '0 →'.
'De Rham' is written 'DeRham'; 'lisse' is a superscript insertion after 'relatif'.
